title: In the image (Genesis 1:26–27)
hookLine: every person is made in God's image; the rabbis say a king's coins look alike, but God's people never do (Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5)

cards: Take two coins of the same kind. Same face on both, a president or a queen, down to the last line of the hair. That's the point of a coin: stamped from one die, identical, interchangeable.
Nobody cares which quarter they get. Now think of any ten people. Not one of them is the same.
Nearly two thousand years ago, the rabbis put those two facts side by side, and made them one of the boldest teachings in Jewish law.

teach.h: TZELEM ELOHIM — THE IMAGE OF GOD.
teach.b: On the sixth day, the Torah slows down.

teach.h: WHAT IS THE IMAGE? IT DOESN'T SAY.
teach.b: In the Jewish Publication Society's 1917 translation: "And God created man in His own image, in the image of God created He him; male and female created He them." In Hebrew: tzelem Elohim.
Tzelem is an image, a likeness, the word for a statue or a figure. Elohim is God. Every human being carries God's likeness.
What that likeness is, the Torah doesn't say. Maimonides said the mind, the ability to understand. Others say freedom, the power to choose, or to create, or to love.
Now the coins. The Mishnah, describing how judges warned witnesses in a capital case, puts it this way.

A human king stamps many coins with one seal, and they all look alike. The King of kings stamped every person with the seal of the first human, and not one is like another. God's image makes us different, not the same.
Then it goes further. Why was humanity created from a single person?

teach.h: ONE LIFE IS A WHOLE WORLD.
teach.b: So that whoever destroys one life is as if they destroyed a whole world, and whoever saves one life, as if they saved a whole world. So no one can say to anyone else, my ancestor was greater than yours.

teach.h: IN THE IMAGE OF GOD CREATED HE HIM.
teach.b: And so each person is obliged to say: the world was created for my sake. Two rabbis once argued over the Torah's greatest principle. Rabbi Akiva said: love your neighbor as yourself.
Ben Azzai pointed to the verse about humanity made in God's likeness, and said his was greater, because it covers everyone.

how: Jewish teaching and law draw on tzelem Elohim for the dignity of every person, from the care of the sick to the honor given to the dead; the Mishnah's saying about saving one life as saving a whole world is widely quoted.

practice: Picture a face you passed recently and barely noticed: a cashier, a driver, someone on the street. See it clearly, down to the one detail that's theirs and nobody else's.
If you believe what the verse says, see God's image there; if you don't, see one entire world.

wordCard.voice: Tzelem Elohim. The image of God, stamped on every person, so that no two are alike.

orig.note: Hebrew: the image of God. tzelem is the word for a likeness or figure.

carryVoice: Your line: no two faces alike. One seal, and every face its own. See you tomorrow.
